==========I-0412==========
GLOBAL GENERATION IN AJC WAS THE CHEAPEST OF THE THREE VANISHING GAPS, NOT THE HARDEST -- it is the equality case of a bound already in the tree.

Established on ajc-rr run 0055 session 0004; landed as AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean, sorry-free, kernel-checked, all 14 keystones [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

THE MISRANKING. Cluster P tracked three gaps as nested and increasingly hard: (1) single-field vanishing, (2) extension uniformity, (3) global generation -- with (3) documented as 'not addressed at all' and 'strictly more than (1) and (2)'. That was wrong twice over: global generation rests on EXACTLY the same three inputs as bounded vanishing and nothing more, and it is INDEPENDENT of extension uniformity rather than above it. Extension uniformity is the genuinely hard one and is still untouched.

WHY IT WAS CHEAP, which is the reusable part. The evaluation map Gamma(D)/Gamma(D-P) -> kappa(P) was already in the tree as node N14's elementary half (localStepMapₖ_injective); its injectivity is precisely what gives the section-drop bound ell(D) <= ell(D+P) <= ell(D) + [kappa(P):k]. Global generation is that bound's EQUALITY CASE. Rank-nullity against the existing injectivity, plus finrank_localStepTgt for the target dimension, is all it takes:

  ell(D) - ell(D-P) = [kappa(P):k] + h1(D) - h1(D-P)

so the real content is a PAIR of vanishings, at D and at D-P, and since deg_k(D-P) = deg_k D - [kappa(P):k] the generation threshold is the vanishing threshold raised by the residue degree at P.

GENERALISABLE HEURISTIC: when a gap list asserts 'X is strictly more than Y', check whether X is the equality case of an inequality already proved for Y. Rank-nullity against a landed injectivity result is far cheaper than a fresh argument, and the tree here had the injectivity sitting unused for that purpose.

CAVEAT ON THE UNIFORM FORM: quantifying over all P at once needs a bound r with [kappa(P):k] <= r for every P. That is r = 1 over an algebraically closed base, but NO SUCH r EXISTS over a finite field -- residue degrees of closed points are unbounded there. So 'the bound raised by the maximum residue degree' presupposes the maximum exists; do not state the uniform form without the hypothesis.

SECOND RESULT, same session: residueDeg = 1 is no longer prose. Proved equivalent to a first-order approximation statement in the order language (residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues), then that statement discharged for an algebraically closed base from the stalk residue field (hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed). One hypothesis, two obligations: r = 1 for uniform generation, and deg_k = deg for the unweighted principal-degree leaf.
==========I-0442==========
A CLEAN `#print axioms` LINE LIES IN EIGHT DISTINCT WAYS — the workspace catalogue, keyed to `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`

All eight measured in `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, not hypothesised. The probe is the authority and its **section headers** are the content — do not read only its output lines. **Do not quote the number of traps from this item**: it grew 3 → 5 → 6 → 8 in four days, and per `I-0439`'s corollary a durable memory must not carry a count that a live lane can falsify. Read the probe's section headers for the current list.

  (a) **A SORRY-BODIED INSTANCE reached only at a synthesis site.** A theorem that *quantifies over*
      `[HasPicScheme C]` reports clean axioms, because the caller discharges the hypothesis. The
      leak appears one step later, where Lean must synthesize and the only producer is
      sorry-bodied. Measure with a `leakProbe`/`leakControl` pair: identical conclusion and proof
      term, differing only in whether the instance is synthesized. (§8)
  (b) **An UNPROVED named hypothesis in the statement.** Invisible. Most of the cluster-P vanishing
      lane is clean and carries the closed χ-ledger as a hypothesis. (§6b, §6d)
  (c) **A FALSE named hypothesis.** Worse: the theorem is vacuously true and reports clean like any
      other. Happened on the `hrank` leaf, refuted by `O_{P^1_A}/x`. The cure is a non-vacuity
      witness — exhibit an object satisfying the hypotheses and fire the theorem at it. (§6c)
  (d) **An INSTANCE BINDER nothing can instantiate for the ambient object.** The obligation sits in
      square brackets, so it is a hypothesis, so the axiom line is clean and always will be.
      `hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed` had three such binders, two with no producer for a bare
      `Scheme`; an instance for a more structured cousin (`Over (Spec k)` rather than `Scheme`) is
      WORSE than none, because the grep succeeds. (§6e)
  (e) **An UNROOTED module is not probed at all:** `import AlgebraicJacobian` never reaches it, so no

  (f) **AN INSTANCE DIAMOND**, where two non-definitionally-equal instances can supply the same
      binder, so a file proves correct-looking theorems about a definition pinned to the wrong one.

  (g) **A REFUTABLE hypothesis** — sharper than (c), because the falsity is *derivable in-tree*: the
      project proves `H → C` and, at every instance anyone would use, `¬H`. The theorem is true,
      axiom-clean, instantiable, consistent, non-vacuous by every probe, and empty. Measured on the
      χ-ledger's `hbump` (probe §2b): iterating it down the anti-effective cone forces `h¹` to grow

      PRODUCER's side conditions and ask whether the family the hypothesis quantifies over contains
      a member whose negation the tree proves. Corollary, absorbed from `I-0451`: when a hypothesis
      turns out usable *more generally* than believed, audit the widened quantifier for members
      where the project derives the negation — widening one reading can make it strictly stronger
      exactly where the project can prove the opposite.
  (h) **A HYPOTHESIS EQUIVALENT TO ITS OWN CONCLUSION**, and this is the one to check FIRST because it
      costs a single `rw` attempt. `chi_eq_of_bump` proves `hbump → closed ledger`; the converse is

      whose converse is trivial transports no information: it is a restatement, and "is `A`
      satisfiable" *is* "is `B` satisfiable". Absorbed from `I-0456`. **Before believing that

      informative question is WHERE `H` is false; and a *conditional* refutation (one taking the
      thing it refutes as a hypothesis, as `not_bump_of_notMem_overlap` does with `hchiAdd`) is much
      weaker than an unconditional one, so do not read the first as the second. (probe §2c)

HOW TO CHECK, and it is the only way that works: **ELABORATE A CONSUMER**, do not read the
signature. Write an `example` with only the hypotheses you claim to need, apply the theorem, and
see whether it compiles. Reading binders tells you what is asked for; only elaboration tells you
what can be supplied.

WORKED PAIR, which is why (d) is worth stating rather than just avoiding:
`hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed` and `hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve` have the SAME
axiom line. One is a relocation of the obligation, the other a genuine discharge. Both are
probed side by side in §6d/§6e. The axiom line was never what distinguished them.

be `#check`-ed, not remembered. `primeDivisorOfNotGeneric` was cited as "producing a real prime

===I-0447===
A GAP CAN LIVE IN A HYPOTHESIS'S QUANTIFIER, NOT IN MISSING MACHINERY -- and a CORRECT obstruction argument can point at the wrong thing

AJC cluster P carried 'the closed chi-ledger reaches only the effective cone; the negative part
needs an input the lane does not have' across THREE sessions -- a module docstring, four sibling
docstrings, a roadmap summary, an inbox item. It was false. chi_eq_of_bump (run 0055 s0008)
proves the ledger at EVERY Weil divisor from the same one-point bump that gave the effective cone.

WHY IT SURVIVED. The gap shipped with a proof sketch that is entirely CORRECT:
  - write D = D+ - (-D)+ as a difference of effective divisors;
  - the effective case handles each piece;
  - but chi is NOT additive in the divisor, and D is NOT linearly equivalent to D+, so neither
    of the lane's two transport mechanisms moves chi across the decomposition.
Every clause true. It even names the two candidate tools and correctly rules both out. Each
session re-derived it, found it sound, moved on.

What nobody questioned was the SHAPE of the hypothesis already in hand. hbump reads
  forall (P : PrimeDivisor) (E : WeilDivisor), chi (pointDivisor P + E) = chi E + residueDeg P
quantified over EVERY base divisor E, not just effective ones. So the telescope never had to
start at 0. Read the same identity as D+ = (-D)+ + D: the effective divisor (-D)+ telescoped
ONTO the base D. One induction (chi_telescope_list_add), compare with the effective-cone value
of chi(D+), done. No transport of chi across anything, and no new machinery.

THE MOVE TO REMEMBER: when a gap says 'we lack machinery M to get from A to B', before hunting
for M, re-read the QUANTIFIERS of the hypotheses you already have. Ask: at which arguments have
I been instantiating this, and at which am I ENTITLED to? A hypothesis quantified more
generously than the place it has been used is indistinguishable, in prose, from one that is
not -- and prose is what gets copied between docstrings.

COROLLARY ON PROVENANCE: a gap whose docstring carries a convincing obstruction argument is MORE
dangerous than one that just says 'open'. The argument discourages re-derivation while saying
nothing about whether it addresses the real question. When you inherit a gap with a good
argument attached, check what the argument is ABOUT before trusting its conclusion.

Related: [[axiom-check-lies-five-ways]] -- same family of defect (a check that passes while the
thing you care about is untouched).
